base.description: Sprint 24 verified released master: v0.0.155 published and verified, records and release tooling merged via PR #48

candidateRoot.reason: Sprint 24 produced two different artifact builds from one identical source in two different roots and the cause was never established. Choosing the root up front keeps the promoted artifact and its native evidence in the same root.

version.evidence: git ls-remote --tags shows v0.0.150 through v0.0.155 and no v0.0.156; the GitHub release list ends at v0.0.155 (Latest)
version.note: Not assumed from the order; re-confirm immediately before publication.

sourceContract.edition: Pathfinder First Edition adult monster entries and summon tables

brachiosaurus.strengthRoutine: one natural weapon: native 1.5x on a positive modifier (13 * 1.5 = 19, matching the printed 4d6+19); correct x1 at zero or a penalty
brachiosaurus.trampleDerivation: damage 1.5x Str (2d6+19); DC 10 + floor(HD/2)=9 + Str mod 13 = 32

tailBonusDiscrepancy.corroboration: the same inputs independently derive both printed maneuver values: CMB +30 = 13 + 13 + 4 Gargantuan, and CMD 40 = 10 + 13 + 13 + 0 Dex + 4
tailBonusDiscrepancy.rejectedAlternative: +22 would require an unexplained -1 that no printed input supplies
prohibited: asserting that the two sources agree
tailBonusDiscrepancy.authority: owner instruction of 2026-10-15; stands unless an authoritative erratum

brachiosaurus.featAuditRule: reuse qualified behaviour where supported; document an actual unsupported consumer; existing Improved Overrun limitations do not silently authorize omitting a different mandatory feat

elephant.strengthRoutine: two primary natural attacks: x1 Strength each (+10 from Str 30), NOT Brachiosaurus's lone-tail 1.5x handling
elephant.reachRule: space 15 ft but printed reach 10 ft; do not generalise 15-ft reach to every Huge creature
forbidden: suppressing an already released Elephant route
changing actual Mastodon units or assets
elephant.d8TrampleReuse: reuse the exact Sprint 23 d8 trample support

rootShape.rule: a creature whose base tier is T gets one root at T, 1d3 at T+1, and 1d4+1 at each level from T+2 through 9
rootShape.verifiedAgainst: Sprint 24: Deinonychus base tier 4 produced 6 roots per list (4,5,6,7,8,9) and Tyrannosaurus base tier 7 produced 3 per list (7,8,9); the native route census observed exactly 18 routes

expectedIfNatureAllyOnly.source: the order's stated expectation, arithmetically self-consistent

expectedIfBothLists.alsoAdds: celestial/fiendish execution children on the Monster rows
expectedIfBothLists.source: the printed Summon Monster VII table and the project roster catalog

escalatedDecision.question: Does Brachiosaurus get three roots on Summon Nature's Ally VII only, as the order states, or six roots across both Summon Monster VII and Nature's Ally VII, as the printed table and the project roster catalog indicate?
escalatedDecision.orderText: Brachiosaurus is new: SNA VII only, three roots (VII one, VIII 1d3, IX 1d4+1), no Monster row and no celestial/fiendish execution children.
conflictingEvidence: The Summon Monster VII 7th-level list prints "Brachiosaurus (dinosaur)*" alongside Dire crocodile*, Dire shark*, Giant squid*, Mastodon (elephant)*, Roc* and Tyrannosaurus (dinosaur)*.

src/KingmakerGunslinger/Summoning/ExpandedSummoningIdealRosterCatalog.cs records R("brachiosaurus","Brachiosaurus",7,7,25,...) - monster tier 7 AND nature's ally tier 7 - in the same two-tier shape that gives Summon-Monster-only outsiders such as Vrock and Xill a null nature's ally tier.
Sprint 24's Tyrannosaurus, also recorded 7 / 7, was published on both lists.
escalatedDecision.whyBlockingForThisPart: Identities are allocated once and append-only, and the root structure determines the identity allocation, the execution children, the published surface counts and the native route census. Implementing the wrong one cannot be cleanly withdrawn.
